company_name: Joint Stock Company Kaspi.kz (Frankfurt EUR line; primary listing Nasdaq: KSPI)
sector: Emerging Market Fintech / Digital Super App (Payments, E-Commerce Marketplace, Consumer & SME Lending)
overview: Kaspi.kz operates Kazakhstan's dominant consumer and merchant "Super App," combining Payments, an e-Commerce/Marketplace platform, and a Fintech (lending/deposits/insurance) platform used by more than 26 million consumers and 900 thousand merchants. Since acquiring ~65-87% of Turkish e-commerce platform Hepsiburada in January 2025 (and its banking arm, since rebranded Hepsi Bank, in mid-2026), Kaspi has expanded into Türkiye as a second growth market. The company is incorporated in Kazakhstan, primary-listed on Nasdaq (KSPI, since January 2024) with legacy LSE GDRs (since 2020) and this secondary, thinly-traded Frankfurt EUR line (KKS.F); all financial reporting is in Kazakhstani tenge (KZT).

business_model.summary: Kaspi earns money across three tightly integrated platforms: Payments (transaction/take-rate fees on a large QR/card/P2P/B2B payments network, plus float/interest income), Marketplace (e-commerce and m-commerce take rates on GMV plus fast-growing value-added services -- advertising, delivery, classifieds), and Fintech (net interest income and fees from consumer/BNPL/merchant/car loans funded largely by retail deposits). Cross-selling within the Super App (single login, one wallet, integrated checkout/financing at point of sale) drives high monthly engagement (77 transactions per active consumer in Kazakhstan) and blends transactional (Payments), recurring subscription-like usage (Marketplace/advertising) and balance-sheet-based (Fintech lending/deposits) revenue.

revenue_streams.name: Fintech (loans, deposits, insurance)
revenue_streams.trend: growing, margin pressured by high KZT rates/funding costs

revenue_streams.name: Payments
revenue_streams.trend: stable, capital-light, take-rate mix shift down

business_model.customer_type: B2C mass-market consumers plus B2B/SME merchants; largely unbanked/underbanked and offline-to-online migrating retail population in Kazakhstan, expanding to Türkiye
business_model.geographic_mix: Kazakhstan and Other ~75-80% of FY2025 revenue; Türkiye (Hepsiburada/Hepsi Bank) ~20-25% and rising following the January 2025 acquisition and 2026 bank buildout

main_competitors: Freedom Holding Corp / Freedom Bank (digital finance/brokerage rival)
Wildberries/other regional e-commerce entrants in Kazakhstan
Trendyol (Alibaba-backed) and other e-commerce players in Türkiye
competitive_position.market_position: Dominant Super App and largest fintech/e-commerce ecosystem in Kazakhstan by users, GMV and TPV; a newer, still-subscale challenger position in Türkiye via its ~87% stake in Hepsiburada, competing against larger incumbents (Trendyol) in a market roughly 5x Kazakhstan's population

moat_factors.description: Single app and wallet linking 26m+ consumers and 900k+ merchants across payments, shopping and credit creates two-sided network effects and high engagement (77 transactions/month)
Proprietary transaction and behavioral data across payments/e-commerce enables fast, low-cost consumer and merchant credit decisions, a structural edge over traditional banks

Kaspi is the default financial and shopping app for a large share of Kazakhstan's population; rapid adoption of new products (Kaspi Alaqan pay-by-palm registered ~a third of Almaty's adults in under 3 months; Kasper AI assistant used by ~20% of eligible consumers within a month)
Digital-first infrastructure keeps incremental unit economics favorable versus branch-based banks, though Fintech funding costs are balance-sheet intensive
Long-standing offline merchant relationships support conversion to e-Commerce (e.g., Shoes & Clothing GMV +103% YoY as merchants migrate from m-Commerce)

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on the Kazakhstan macro/regulatory environment for the large majority of profit
Hepsiburada/Türkiye still loss-making to breakeven with a wide engagement gap versus Kazakhstan (purchases per consumer 6.7 vs 24.8; GMV per consumer ~1.6x lower)
Complex multi-jurisdiction, multi-currency reporting (KZT/TRY/USD) that obscures underlying growth and requires company-provided "underlying" adjustments
Reputational overhang from 2024 short-seller sanctions allegations and ongoing US securities class-action litigation
Concentrated founder/insider ownership creates governance and periodic share-sale overhang risk

growth_drivers: Hepsiburada/Türkiye expansion: consumer/merchant base growth, engagement-gap closure versus Kazakhstan, and from 2027 a new Fintech (lending/deposits) layer via the newly acquired and capitalized Hepsi Bank (~$300m capital commitment)
e-Commerce migration from m-Commerce in Kazakhstan, with e-Grocery GMV growing >40-50% YoY and continuing to scale
Advertising and other Value-Added Services (delivery, classifieds) monetizing the Marketplace at a much faster rate than GMV growth, lifting take rates
Kasper, Kaspi's AI shopping assistant launched July 2026, aimed at deepening engagement and conversion, with plans to extend beyond shopping to more Super App tasks
Kaspi Alaqan (pay-by-palm) biometric payments rollout nationwide during 2026, extending the payments moat and reducing reliance on cards/phones
Government services and cross-border/payments expansion embedded in the Super App, deepening daily utility and stickiness
Potential interest-rate tailwind: Kazakhstan inflation moderating could allow National Bank rate cuts, which management flags as a meaningful future profit driver not currently assumed in guidance
M&A option value: management has articulated an ambition to become a "100 million user" company across multiple countries, implying further international expansion beyond Türkiye

business.description: Integration, consumer-engagement gap closure, and path to profitability remain unproven; management explicitly manages Hepsiburada to only around Adjusted EBITDA breakeven near-term
Freedom Holding/Freedom Bank and traditional banks are investing in digital rails in Kazakhstan; Trendyol and others are entrenched in Türkiye e-commerce
2025 Kazakh government smartphone import registration rules caused a supply disruption that depressed Marketplace GMV/net income for several quarters

business.risk: Reliance on continued Super App engagement
business.description: Growth model depends on maintaining/deepening the ~77 monthly transactions per active consumer; any degradation in UX, trust, or AI rollout (Kasper) could slow monetization

financial.description: Average deposit cost of funding rose ~150bps YoY to 14.5% in 2Q 2026 amid Kazakhstan's high-rate environment, compressing Fintech and consolidated net income margins even as revenue grows strongly

All reporting is in KZT; Türkiye results are translated from TRY, and the ~21% YoY depreciation of the Turkish lira versus the tenge in 2Q 2026 materially reduced reported e-Commerce/Marketplace growth. On top of this, the Frankfurt (KKS.F) line trades in EUR against KZT-denominated fundamentals and a USD-quoted primary listing (Nasdaq), adding a further currency-translation layer and potential valuation mismatch/liquidity risk for EUR investors
~$300 million committed to capitalize Hepsi Bank, plus ongoing Hepsiburada investment, while resuming dividends -- balance sheet flexibility must fund growth, dividends and buybacks simultaneously
NPL ratio rose to 7.0% in 6M 2026 versus 6.1% in FY2025, and cost of risk ticked up to 0.7% in 2Q 2026 from 0.6%, even though management characterizes underlying credit trends as stable

regulatory.description: Kazakhstan raised the corporate tax rate on banks from 20% to 25% (ex-business lending) effective 2026, adding ~200bps to Kaspi's consolidated tax rate
National Bank of Kazakhstan raised minimum reserve requirements in August 2025 with a further step-up expected April 2026, reducing interest income capacity

Kazakhstan enforces a 46% all-in interest rate cap on consumer loans, with 2026 proposals to move toward risk-based pricing and potentially tighten caps further (toward ~40%), which could pressure Fintech yields
Class actions filed after the September 2024 short-seller report alleging sanctions violations and misleading disclosures around the Nasdaq listing remain a legal overhang

Operating simultaneously under Kazakh, Turkish and US (SEC/Nasdaq foreign private issuer) regulatory regimes increases compliance complexity, especially as Hepsi Bank scales lending/deposits in Türkiye from 2027

macro.description: Culper Research's September 2024 report alleged Kaspi facilitated Russia-linked payment flows and misrepresented its Russia exposure ahead of its Nasdaq listing; Kaspi disputed the report as misleading, but the allegations (and related lawsuit claims of sanctions violations) remain a geopolitical tail risk given Kazakhstan's proximity to and trade relationships with Russia

Kazakhstan's currency and macro conditions (inflation, interest rates, oil-linked terms of trade) directly drive Kaspi's funding costs and consumer spending power; the KZT/USD and KZT/TRY cross-rates also drive material translation effects on reported growth
Hepsiburada's results are exposed to TRY depreciation and high domestic inflation, requiring inflation-adjusted "underlying" metrics to interpret true growth

High Kazakh policy rates are currently a profit headwind (higher deposit costs); a future rate-cutting cycle (inflation moderating) is flagged by management as a potential tailwind not yet in guidance -- a two-way macro sensitivity
Broader Central Asian political and economic stability, and Kazakhstan's relationships with Russia, China and the West, remain a background risk for a business almost entirely dependent on the region

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Kazakhstan's digital payments, e-commerce and consumer fintech penetration continue to grow from a low base, supporting double-digit sector growth; Türkiye's e-commerce market is larger but more competitive, with Kaspi targeting engagement-driven share gains at Hepsiburada
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate — consumer discretionary (Marketplace) and credit (Fintech) exposure make the business sensitive to Kazakh/Turkish consumer spending and credit cycles, partially offset by resilient, high-frequency Payments usage
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High — Kaspi is a net deposit-funded lender, so Kazakh policy rate moves directly affect funding costs and Fintech margins; a rate-cutting cycle would be a meaningful tailwind, a further hiking cycle a headwind
key_input_costs: Delivery/logistics costs for e-Commerce and e-Grocery
Regulatory/compliance costs across Kazakhstan, Türkiye and US listing requirements

recent_developments.event: Q2/H1 2026 results: revenue +15% YoY to $2.3B, adjusted EBITDA +5% to $826M, net income roughly flat at $539M on higher funding costs and Türkiye investment; board proposed an 18% dividend increase to KZT1,000/ADS; full-year 2026 guidance reiterated

Completed acquisition of Rabobank A.Ş. in Türkiye, rebranded Hepsi Bank; launched a pilot shopping loan integrated into Hepsiburada using the micro-finance license, with plans to expand Fintech offerings in Türkiye from 2027 (~$300m capitalization commitment)

Began rollout of Kasper, an AI personal shopping assistant, to all Kazakhstan e-Commerce consumers; ~20% of eligible consumers used it within a month, with ~80% of conversations producing a tailored recommendation

Tencent, CEO Mikheil Lomtadze, senior management and long-term US institutional investors (including university endowments) purchased 6.0 million ADSs from Baring Fintech Venture Funds; Tencent became one of Kaspi's largest shareholders, with Morgan Stanley advising

Co-founder/major shareholder Vyacheslav Kim sold roughly 1 million ADSs (~$86.7m) under a pre-arranged 10b5-1 trading plan dated December 2025, reducing his stake from ~20.75% to ~20.06%; still Kaspi's second-largest shareholder behind Lomtadze (~23%)

Q4/FY2025 results: FY2025 revenue +19% YoY (KZT4.05T/$8.0B including Türkiye), net income +10% YoY; board recommended resuming a quarterly dividend of KZT850/ADS; management introduced Adjusted EBITDA guidance (including Türkiye for the first time) of ~5% YoY growth for 2026, citing bank tax rate increase (20%→25%), higher minimum reserve requirements, and continued near-breakeven management of Hepsiburada as headwinds
Launched Kaspi Alaqan (pay-by-palm) in Almaty; ~500,000 consumers (roughly a third of the city's adult population) registered within 3 months, with ~9% transaction penetration where available

Culper Research published a short-seller report alleging Kaspi facilitated Russia-sanctions-evading payment flows and misrepresented Russia exposure ahead of its Nasdaq listing; shares fell as much as ~23% before partially recovering; Kaspi disputed the report as misleading and inaccurate; a US securities class action followed on behalf of investors who bought shares between January and September 2024

guidance.as_of: Q2 2026 Results (10 August 2026), reiterating FY2025 results guidance (2 March 2026)

items.metric: GMV (Marketplace/e-Commerce, constant currency, pro-forma incl. Türkiye)
items.notes: H1 2026 actual GMV growth of +17% tracking toward the full-year target
H1 2026 actual +20%; management now guides average net loan portfolio rather than TFV as the more representative Fintech growth metric given mix/duration shift toward longer-tenor loans

H1 2026 actual +7%; guidance assumes constant currency (rates as of 1 January 2026), reflects higher bank tax rate, higher minimum reserve requirements, high domestic interest rates, and deliberately near-breakeven management of Hepsiburada; does not assume any Kazakh rate cuts, which management flags as potential future upside not currently modeled

items.target: KZT 1,000 per ADS, up 18% from KZT 850
items.notes: Dividends were resumed in Q4 2025 results (KZT850/ADS) after a hiatus tied to the Hepsiburada acquisition; management describes the increase as reflecting confidence in long-term growth and strong H1 2026 cash generation

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Mikheil Lomtadze's letters frame strategy around three pillars: (1) balancing Türkiye investment with resumed/growing dividends, now feasible post-Hepsiburada integration; (2) closing Hepsiburada's large engagement gap versus Kazakhstan (purchases per consumer 6.7 vs 24.8) as the #1 Türkiye growth lever, while deliberately managing it to near-EBITDA-breakeven in the near term; and (3) absorbing known 2026 Kazakhstan headwinds (bank tax hike to 25%, higher reserve requirements, high funding costs) while positioning for a potential rate-cut tailwind not yet assumed in guidance. Management also emphasizes Kasper (AI shopping assistant, launched July 2026) and Kaspi Alaqan (pay-by-palm) as the next wave of engagement-driven growth, and reiterated an ambition to become a '100 million user' company across multiple countries.

bull_case: Dominant, highly engaged Super App in Kazakhstan (77 monthly transactions/consumer) with genuine two-sided network effects across payments, e-commerce and credit that are difficult for competitors to replicate

e-Commerce/Marketplace VAS (advertising, delivery) monetization is scaling much faster than GMV (constant-currency VAS +49% YoY vs e-Commerce revenue +35% in Q2 2026), expanding take rates and margins

Large, underpenetrated Türkiye opportunity via Hepsiburada plus the newly acquired Hepsi Bank, which could replicate Kaspi's Kazakhstan fintech playbook from 2027 onward if the consumer-engagement gap narrows
Resumed and now growing dividend (+18% to KZT1,000/ADS) alongside continued double-digit revenue growth signals confidence in cash generation even while funding Türkiye investment

Credible new engagement/monetization levers (Kasper AI shopping assistant, Kaspi Alaqan pay-by-palm) show continued product innovation and fast early adoption, and high-profile new shareholders (Tencent, alongside the CEO) signal strategic and institutional confidence
Potential Kazakh interest-rate-cut tailwind (inflation moderating) is not yet reflected in FY2026 guidance, representing optionality on margins
bear_case: Hepsiburada/Türkiye remains loss-making to at best EBITDA-breakeven, with heavy ongoing capital commitments (~$300m for Hepsi Bank) and an unproven path to closing the large engagement/profitability gap versus Kazakhstan

2026 Kazakhstan-specific headwinds are structural, not transitory: bank corporate tax raised from 20% to 25%, minimum reserve requirements stepping up again in April 2026, and elevated deposit funding costs (cost of funding +150bps YoY to 14.5% in Q2 2026) are compressing net income growth well below revenue growth

Unresolved reputational and legal overhang from the September 2024 Culper short-seller report alleging Russia-sanctions exposure, plus an active US securities class action, creates episodic volatility and headline risk

Multi-layered currency exposure (KZT operations, TRY-denominated Türkiye results, USD primary listing, and this EUR-denominated Frankfurt line) adds translation risk and complexity that can obscure underlying operating performance and create valuation/liquidity mismatches for EUR investors on KKS.F specifically, which is a thin, secondary listing

Regulatory tightening risk on consumer lending (potential further reduction of the 46% APR cap toward ~40%, shift to risk-based pricing) could directly pressure Fintech yields, Kaspi's largest and highest-margin segment

Continued insider share sales by major shareholders (e.g., Vyacheslav Kim's ~$87m in sales during March-June 2026), even under pre-arranged trading plans, can weigh on sentiment given concentrated founder ownership
